Open Start and type your company name and your own targets in the yellow cells: cash-on-cash, DSCR, cap rate, the highest cost ratio, the budget tolerance and the rent gap that needs action.

Fill Property months each month with the rent collected, each cost and the loan payments for every property. NOI (rent collected minus operating costs, before loan payments) and cash flow fill in, and a negative cash flow turns red.
Read Property results: the last 12 months of each held property give NOI, cap rate, cash-on-cash, DSCR, return on equity, a rank and the keep, fix or sell signal.
Keep Underwriting up to date with the rent, the vacancy and the costs used at purchase, and Cash invested with the cash you put in. The results compare the real year with them.
Set a yearly budget for each property on Budget by property and enter the actual cost; the variance and a check show where costs run over.
Use Expenses, Rent payments, Loan payments, Loans and Valuations as the records behind the numbers; Expense ratios and Benchmarks show each cost as a share of rent against your own targets.
Check Rent against market for every unit: the gap to the market rent for a month and for a year shows where rent is left on the table. Check your own local rules before you change a rent.
Write every finding on the Action list with an owner and a due date, rate each property on Performance reviews and note rate and value changes on Rate and value changes.

Use the 14 calculators: property result, cash-on-cash, actual against underwriting, expense ratio, cost savings, value from NOI, rent increase, vacancy, keep fix or sell, return on equity, break-even rent, a rate rise, ranking and a grid.
Read the Property Performance Dashboard and Charts every month: NOI, cash flow, DSCR, cost ratios, budget variance, rent gap and open actions.

Properties: cost, value, equity and exit plan
The 16 properties with price, value and exit plan; total cost, cost basis (price plus improvements), loan balance, equity, LTV (loan divided by value) and cash from a sale fill in.
Cash from a sale before tax
One row for each loan; the payment, the balance today, the loan payments of a year, LTV and the days to a balloon (a loan whose remaining balance is due on one date) fill in.
One row for each opinion of value with the source; the gain against the total cost of the property fills in.
Net worth by quarter: value, loans and cash
One row for each quarter with the value of all properties, the loan balances and the cash; net worth (what you own minus what you owe), the change since the last quarter and the target fill in.
Equity by property: value, loan, equity and LTV
One row for each held property; the value, the loan balance, the equity, the LTV, the share of all equity and the room to borrow at your highest LTV fill in from Properties and Loans.
Depreciation: yearly rows for the tax package
One row for each property and tax year with the cost basis, the depreciation, the rent income, the costs and the interest; the taxable estimate fills in (check with your own adviser).
Basis adjustments: what changes the cost basis
One row for each improvement, extra rehab, fee or insurance payout after the purchase; the effect on the cost basis and the new adjusted basis of the property fill in.
Depreciation schedule: yearly amount, taken and remaining
One row for each held property with the date placed in service; the building cost, the yearly depreciation, the amount taken so far and the amount remaining fill in (check with your own adviser).
Sales: what each past sale made
One row for each past sale with the price, the costs and the profit; the hold days, the return on the cost and the estimated tax set-aside fill in (check with your own adviser).
Exit analyses: net cash from each exit option
One row for each look at selling, refinancing or exchanging; net proceeds (price minus loan payoff, costs and estimated tax) fill in. Check with your own adviser.
Hold against sell: return on equity by property
One row for each held property; the return on equity (cash flow plus value gain, divided by equity), the cash from a sale or a refinance and a signal fill in.
Exchange timeline: the dates to act on
One row for each sale you may exchange; the day to name a replacement, the day to close, the days left and a check fill in. Day counts are in Settings: use the ones your own adviser gives you.
Sale plans: list date, price and cash in hand
One row for each plan to sell with the list date, price and lowest price; selling costs, loan payoff, estimated tax and net cash fill in. Check with your own adviser.
Tax set-asides: cash kept back for tax
One row for each quarter with the amount you keep back for tax and why; whether it is paid in and a check fill in. These are estimates: check with your own adviser.
Tax summary by year and town: income, costs and depreciation
One row for each year and town from the Depreciation page; the taxable estimate (income less costs, interest and depreciation) fills in. A minus is a paper loss. Ask your adviser.
Adviser questions: what to ask and what was answered
One row for each question for your accountant or adviser with the answer; open or answered, the days waiting and a check fill in. Only open questions can be late.
Growth targets: net worth each quarter
One row for each quarter with the net worth you aim for; the net worth you reached fills in from Net worth by quarter.
Agent opinions of value: the agent view over time
One row for each opinion of value from your agent; the gap to the value now, the age in days and a current or old check fill in.
